summary.tagline: Explore subterranean waterfalls, ancient stalactites, and Bronze Age history in the Upper Swansea Valley.
summary.seo_title: Visiting Dan-yr-Ogof: National Showcaves Centre for Wales

travel.headline: Advance Ticket Booking for the National Showcaves Centre
travel.reservation: Entry is managed via a single ticket covering the three primary showcaves and above-ground attractions. While entry permits are not required for the surrounding National Nature Reserve, visitors should check the official website for current ticketing procedures and seasonal opening dates as access is subject to site operations.

days.title: Subterranean Wonders of the Swansea Valley

stops.name: Dan-yr-Ogof
stops.detail: Walk through 315 million years of geological history featuring winding passageways and thousands of unique stalactites.

stops.name: Cathedral Cave
stops.detail: Witness the massive Dome of St Paul's cavern and underground waterfalls within this expansive chamber.

stops.name: Bone Cave
stops.detail: Explore the site where 42 Bronze Age skeletons were discovered, providing a glimpse into ancient human history.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes from the coast; conditions vary based on local valley traffic.
days.note: All three caves are included on one ticket; pace your visit to allow time for the above-ground Iron Age village.

intel.title: On-site Facilities
intel.text: Designated parking is available at the National Showcaves Centre entrance. Verify capacity and any seasonal restrictions directly with the operator before arrival.

intel.title: Valley Connectivity
intel.text: Mobile signal can be inconsistent in the Upper Swansea Valley. Download navigation maps and booking confirmations before entering the National Nature Reserve area.

intel.title: Local Services
intel.text: Fuel services are limited in the immediate vicinity of the caves. It is recommended to refuel in larger towns like Swansea or Ystradgynlais before heading into the Brecon Beacons.

intel.title: Cave Temperatures
intel.text: The underground environment maintains a consistent cool temperature regardless of surface weather. Plan for a multi-hour visit to cover all three cave systems and the museum.

intel.title: Nature Reserve Entry
intel.text: The caves are located within a National Nature Reserve. Stay on marked paths when exploring the stone circles and outdoor dinosaur park areas.

plan.arrival: Collect your rental in Swansea and drive north into the Brecon Beacons; check in at local valley accommodation before the caves open.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are suitable for the paved valley roads; check RV length restrictions for smaller rural lanes in the Brecon Beacons.
plan.goldenHour: The Upper Swansea Valley viewpoints offer scenic light in late afternoon, though cave interiors are artificially lit.
